35.00518,-80.20268: Leonidas L. Polk 1837 1892. President of National Farmers' Alliance, 1889-1892; began Progressive Farmer, 1886; a founder of NCSU and Meredith College. Was born here.
35.19518,-80.11285: Fight At Colson's. Colonel William Lee Davidson's Whig militia defeated Colonel Samuel Bryan's Tories, in July, 1780, a few miles S.E.
35.27051,-80.11801: Randall's United Methodist Church. First services held ca. 1785 by Jesse Lee & Bishop Asbury in home of John Randle. Fifth building, 1974, 3/4 mile East.
35.39892,-80.43557: Mont Amoena Seminary. Lutheran school for girls, 1859-1927. The name is Latin for "Mt. Pleasant." Site is one block south.
35.39916,-80.43574: Mount Pleasant Collegiate Institute. Lutheran junior college for men, 1903-33, on site of North Carolina College, 1853-1902. Two blocks north.
35.40711,-80.11592: L'aluminium Francais. French company in 1913 began Narrows Dam and town named for Adrien Badin, president Southern Aluminum, a subsidiary. Office stood 1/2 mi. N.W.
35.41025,-80.11497: Hardaway Site. Archaeological site key to understanding earliest native population. Its occupation dates to ca. 10,000 B.C. One mi. N.E.
35.41618,-80.47697: St. John's Church. Lutheran. Began ca. 1745 as Dutch Buffalo Creek Church. Adolph Nussman was first regular pastor, 1773. Building erected 1845. 300 yards north.
35.43946,-80.3693: Bethel United Church Of Christ. Began 1745 as Dutch Buffalo Creek Church. German Reformed & Lutheran, 1806-1875. Present structure, 1929, is 2 miles East.
35.47162,-80.26742: Barringer Mine. Gold discovery in 1825 by Mathias Barringer launched the state's subsurface gold mining industry. Site 2 mi. W.
35.48397,-80.28391: Pfeiffer University. Methodist. Founded as Oberlin Home & School near Lenoir, 1885. Moved here, 1910. Renamed for Pfeiffer family, 1935.
